requirement:
Building the book follows {cite}`requirements.index.render_only`.
Coverage documentation is rendered from source annotations and stored review
results without reading saved execution measurements, evaluating exception
acceptance, or auditing review freshness.
rationale: The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.render_only`. All three are marked {test} for the subject. **1. Render from annotations and stored reviews.** - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[overview_shows_missing_unreadable_and_recorded_reviews_with_current_justifications]` renders a source item with a cited annotation. It checks that the current source justification and the stored review are shown. - It runs missing, true, false, FIXME, invalid-JSON and unreadable (directory) review states. It asserts each recorded label, rationale and FIXME text. - The assertion that the review file is byte-identical after rendering shows the review is only read. **2. Do not read saved execution measurements.** - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[book_ignores_saved_measurements_and_preserves_artifacts]` renders once with no saved data. It then renders with a recorded attempt, including a test name and hit data, and asserts the chapters are identical. - It asserts the saved test name never appears in any chapter. - It overwrites `attempt.json` with invalid content (`invalid metadata` and `{}`). Rendering still succeeds and gives the same output, the artifacts are untouched, and no selection cache is created. This shows the measurements are not read or parsed. - It also asserts the output omits measurement-derived content such as "Line coverage:", "selected test attempts" and "Test runs and provenance". - `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` runs the real `habeas mdbook` binary after a real coverage capture. A cargo shim fails any cargo call other than `metadata`. The test asserts no test, compile or collection command ran. It also asserts the retained coverage files are unchanged and the output reports no documented gaps. **3. Do not evaluate exception acceptance.** - The overview test records true, false and FIXME determinations. Each renders only as "Recorded review: …". Every case asserts the output does not contain "current and accepted", so a rendered acceptance verdict would be caught. **4. Do not audit review freshness.** - The overview test stores a review with `"old hash"`, and later with no hash or inputs. It then changes the source, both by updating the justification and by removing it. - It asserts the review still shows as "Recorded true" with its saved rationale. It asserts the output does not contain "input is stale", and that the review file is unchanged. - It also checks that the current source justification is shown, so the book is built from current annotations. I found no uncovered obligation, wrong expected result or weak assertion. The cited `requirements.index.render_only` is context, and I did not reassess its tests.

results without reading saved execution measurements, evaluating exception
`habeas mdbook` reads annotations and stored reviews to render their connections.
It does not audit repository evidence, check review freshness or dependency
hashes, enforce reference coverage, or assess citation and site reviews.
It does not load saved execution measurements, run tests, collect coverage,
or invoke an assessment model. Source-input and stored-record read or parse
failures produce readable rendering diagnostics rather than a repository
